brief.audience: Meridian Diagnostics lab director and lab operations lead
brief.decision_maker: The lab director, who decides whether HelixPrep expands beyond one line
brief.purpose: Agree the month 3 test that would let Meridian decide on expansion
brief.ask: Approve a 200+ sample batch test of HelixPrep in month 3
assumptions: The deck is sent ahead and read, not presented; the update is addressed to the lab director, who has not used the unit

story.problem: Meridian wants to run full-volume weeks on HelixPrep, but every batch so far has been under 150 samples, so nobody can say how it behaves at 200 or more.
story.why_care: The lab director decides on expansion and will not recommend it past one line without seeing a full-size batch.
story.solution: Run a 200+ sample batch test in month 3 and judge expansion on that result.
story.why_best: It answers the one condition Meridian has named. Expanding without it would rest on small-batch results. Waiting leaves the decision where it is.
story.thesis: Approve a 200+ sample batch test in month 3, because turnaround and errors have improved at the volumes tested, and the test answers the one condition Meridian has set for expansion.

title.headline: One full-size batch stands between you and expansion
title.subhead: HelixPrep pilot at Meridian Diagnostics, month 3 proposal

exec_summary.headline: Approve a 200+ sample batch test of HelixPrep in month 3
points: The test answers your condition for expansion
exec_summary.open_note: Week 8 turnaround is 65 minutes in the weekly log and 48 minutes in the month 2 update, and the two have not been reconciled.
exec_summary.read: We are asking you to approve a 200+ sample batch test of HelixPrep in month 3. Three things support it. Average turnaround per batch fell from 210 minutes in week 1 to 65 minutes in week 8. Errors fell to zero from week 5 and stayed there. And the test answers the one condition your team has set before recommending expansion past one line. All of the results so far come from batches under 150 samples, which is why the test matters. One figure is still open: the month 2 update reports 48 minutes for week 8, while the weekly log shows 65 minutes. We use the log on these pages and will reconcile the two before the month 3 review.

slides.headline: Your batches are coming through faster each week
slides.subhead: Average turnaround fell from 210 minutes in week 1 to 65 minutes in week 8, at under 150 samples per batch.
slides.claim: Turnaround has fallen steadily at the volumes tested.
points: Update reports a different week 8 figure
slides.read: Turnaround is the measure your team feels first, and it has fallen every week of the pilot. The weekly log shows average turnaround per batch dropping from 210 minutes in week 1 to 65 minutes in week 8. Every one of those batches was under 150 samples, so the trend tells you how HelixPrep behaves at today's volumes and no more. The month 2 update gives 48 minutes for week 8, which does not match the log, and we have not yet reconciled the two. The log is the measured record, so this slide uses it. What the trend cannot show is the full-volume week, which is the question the test answers.

slides.headline: Errors have stopped since the team settled in
slides.subhead: Errors per week fell from 3 in week 1 to 0 from week 5 onward.
slides.claim: Weekly errors fell to zero by week 5 and stayed there.
slides.read: Speed matters only if quality holds, and so far it has. The weekly log shows errors falling from 3 in week 1 to 0 in week 5, and they stayed at zero through week 8. Meridian also reports that both technicians like the new workflow. That is their view rather than a measurement, and we show it as such. Like the turnaround trend, this is evidence at batch sizes under 150 samples. It tells you the process is stable at today's volume, which is the right starting point for testing a larger one. It does not tell you how the unit behaves when a full-volume week arrives, so the next step is to test exactly that.

slides.headline: A 200+ sample test answers your one condition
slides.subhead: Meridian has asked to see a 200+ sample batch before expanding, and nothing above 150 samples has been tested yet.
slides.claim: The only condition Meridian has set for expansion is a 200+ sample batch, which has not been tested.
slides.read: Your team has been clear about what it needs before recommending expansion: to see HelixPrep handle a batch of 200 or more samples. Nothing above 150 samples has been tested, so the results so far cannot answer that question either way. Meridian says the pilot is on track for month 3, which makes month 3 the natural point to run a single full-size batch. We propose agreeing the date and who runs it at the month 3 review, then judging expansion on that result. If turnaround or errors rise at full volume, you will know before committing a second line, not after.

risks.headline: What could still go wrong, and what we would do

items.response: The test measures it directly before any expansion.
We will reconcile the log and the update before month 3.

closing.headline: Approve the full-size batch test so expansion rests on evidence
closing.ask: Approve a 200+ sample batch test in month 3.
